name: Campaign Control Plane
one_liner: The executable portfolio dashboard that turns frozen theses into deterministic checkpoint DAGs and autonomous build experiments.
core_thesis: The correct unit of autonomous software construction is not a repository or a prompt; it is a typed behavioral checkpoint with explicit evidence, a deterministic validator, a dependency position, and an authority class. If each project is decomposed into such checkpoints, autonomous agents can iterate toward externally verifiable functionality while the human only resolves irreducible H-tasks and structural bottlenecks.
why_now: The underlying kernel pieces already exist: ATask records attempts and proof, Seed0 compares seeds, and QP separates cognition, truth and authority. The missing layer is a portfolio/campaign graph that compiles product theses into executable work.
job: See exactly what each project claims, what is proven, what is blocked, what agent should do next, and what only the human can resolve.
distribution: Internal control plane first; later reusable infrastructure for autonomous software factories.
moat: Accumulated validator library, checkpoint ontology, cross-project run data, bottleneck history and empirically learned routing policies.
falsifiers: Behavioral checkpoint decomposition does not reduce false-done rates.
Deterministic evidence is too expensive to capture relative to manual review.
Agent tournaments fail to produce measurable improvement over one guided agent.

success_definition: All 12 checkpoints PROVEN on live evidence, with no unresolved critical H-task or security gate.

repo_binding.polling: GitHub snapshots are implementation evidence only; checkpoint proof comes from validator receipts.

software_substitution_test.counterfactual: OpenAI/platform vendors ship perfect software for every reproducible feature in this project tomorrow.
surviving_value: human decision trajectories when accumulated internally
software_substitution_test.rationale: The control plane is manufacturing infrastructure. Its value is measured by how much scarce-state acquisition it enables, not by defensible software ownership.

underengineer.rule: Choose the earliest real-world event that increases controlled scarce state; build only its prerequisites plus safety and verification.
underengineer.scarce_state_target: Serve one live scarce-asset campaign end-to-end
underengineer.minimal_live_product: One campaign page that can choose a live moat event, dispatch one ATask, ingest independently attested evidence, surface one H-task, and commit one QP receipt.

steps.action: Select one asset campaign and one real moat event
steps.acceptance: A campaign + scarce asset + target event are bound.

steps.action: Dispatch the minimum prerequisite task through ATask
Validate the live outcome with an independent attestation
Commit or refuse the transition through QP
steps.acceptance: Canonical transition receipt or explicit refusal.

underengineer.graduation_rule: One external campaign advances its scarce-asset ledger through this control plane.
underengineer.kill_or_rethink_rule: If it does not reduce human minutes or increase verified scarce-state acquisition for a live campaign, do not extend it.
underengineer.project_manager_invariant: A feature may enter NOW only if it is necessary to reach the first real moat event, required for safety/verification, or empirically unblocks that path.
underengineer.observation_pause: After the first live moat event, stop expanding and inspect customer/outcome evidence before choosing the next feature.

full_roadmap_policy: The original checkpoint ladder is a capability library, not default build order. UNDERENGINEER chooses the live minimum path.

experiment_strategy.learning_goal: Improve allocation/verification; not a demand business.
